knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 \cos{\left(y \right)}}{x \tan{\left(y \right)}}$ for $x\ne 0$ and $-\frac{\pi }{2}<y<\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Also require $y\ne 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2 \cos{\left(y \right)}}{x \tan{\left(y \right)}} \\ (\tan{\left(y \right)} \sec{\left(y \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\tan{\left(y \right)} \sec{\left(y \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y \right)} \sec{\left(y \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y \right)} \sec{\left(y \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \sec{\left(y \right)} & =2 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sec{\left(y \right)}=2 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}+C.
$$
